A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reward-model optimization study. All 54 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original RLHF training experiments, reward-model evaluations, and correlation analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including policy-training outcomes and supplementary reward-model comparisons.

M1.justification: The analyzed RLHF objective, reward-model constructions, and RLOO/GRPO procedures match in both versions. No algorithmic component, loss, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AlpacaFarm and UltraFeedback data for the same supervised-finetuning, preference-modeling, and RLHF tasks. Appendix D introduces no additional coverage relative to v2.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same five reward models trained with different on-policy proportions, perfectly accurate low-variance model, and ground-truth optimization comparator. Section 4.2 and Appendix D.2 retain the same four public reward models in corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, model configurations, normalization schemes, training budgets, and evaluation metrics match. Appendix E retains the same 500-prompt evaluation sample and 10 generated outputs per prompt.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same analyses varying policy size, SFT data, ground-truth reward model, normalization, and policy-gradient method, together with the KL-efficiency comparisons. No ablation, sensitivity test, or supplementary finding is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means across three runs with standard-deviation error bars in Figures 2–3 and preserve the appendix uncertainty reporting. Run-count disclosures and statistical reporting procedures do not change.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and findings in Tables 1–12 and Figures 2–14 match. For example, Table 2 retains reward variance's Pearson correlations of 0.982 with proxy reward increase and 0.834 with ground-truth reward increase.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–3, Theorems 1–6, the Best-of-N proposition in Appendix B, and the derivations and proofs in Appendix C are unchanged. Appendix-reference wording changes do not alter mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: low reward variance impedes RLHF optimization, accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating teachers, and reward-model effectiveness depends on the initial policy.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of reward hacking, KL efficiency, and policy-dependent reward-model effectiveness. The qualifications concerning tabular policies, exact gradients, reward scaling, and other alignment methods also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E preserves the same filtering instructions, chat template, hyperparameters, H100 hardware details, and code/model links. No implementation or access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning match, including Section 5's novelty claim about characterizing how reward-model properties affect policy-gradient optimization. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 replaces references to lettered supplements as 'Section/Sections' with 'Appendix/Appendices' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Minor spacing and wrapping adjustments accompany these edits; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: There are limited caption and typesetting edits, including Figure 11 changing 'Section E.1' to 'Appendix E.1'. Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–12 retain their designs, axes, legends, structures, and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 makes appendix references more precise and provides small typographic adjustments, while preserving the scientific text, proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information. These editorial refinements do not resolve a substantive deficiency or meaningfully change overall paper quality.
